pages.title: Revenue is ahead of plan; churn in small accounts needs a decision
pages.notes: Open with the decision, not the quarter: revenue is ahead of plan, and churn in small accounts is the one thing the board is asked to act on today.
pages.subtitle: Board update, third quarter 2026

pages.title: Revenue is ahead of plan and the board is asked to cut churn
pages.notes: Give the whole update in three sentences: the quarter is ahead, churn in small accounts is the exception, and the ask is one approval. Everything after this page is support.

blocks.lead: Recurring revenue reached EUR 18.4 million, 6% ahead of plan.
points: Gross margin is 78%, one point above plan, with hosting costs flat
Cash stands at EUR 9.4 million, EUR 0.4 million more than planned

blocks.lead: Churn in small accounts doubled in a year, to 4.2% a quarter.
points: Two in five of the accounts lost never finished setting up
Mid-sized and large accounts are as steady as a year ago

blocks.lead: Guided onboarding costs EUR 0.4 million and pays back within 7 months.
points: A pilot with 40 new accounts starts in December
The board sees the result in February and decides on the roll-out

pages.title: This update answers three questions
pages.notes: Name the three questions and say which one needs the board. Move on quickly; nobody needs the agenda explained.

items.name: Results
items.text: Did the quarter meet the plan?

items.name: Customers
items.text: Where are accounts being lost, and why?

items.name: Plan
items.text: What should be done, and what does it cost?

pages.title: Recurring revenue reached EUR 18.4 million in Q3 2026, 6% ahead of plan
pages.notes: Read the highlighted bar first, then the plan beside it. Say what drove the lead over plan in one sentence and stop.
pages.takeaway: Growth came from larger accounts adding seats, not from price.
points: The plan for the quarter was EUR 17.4 million
Net new revenue was EUR 1.1 million against 0.9 planned
List prices have not changed since 2024
pages.alt: Column chart of annual recurring revenue in EUR million for five quarters, rising from 14.1 in Q3 2025 to 18.4 in Q3 2026, 6% ahead of plan.

pages.title: Three figures show a quarter that grew faster than its costs
pages.notes: Take the three figures left to right. The point is the last one: costs grew more slowly than revenue.

figures.label: Annual recurring revenue
figures.note: 30% above the third quarter of 2025, and EUR 1.0 million over plan.

figures.label: Gross margin
figures.note: One point above plan: hosting costs stayed flat while revenue grew.

figures.label: Net revenue retention
figures.note: Customers a year old now spend 4% more, after all churn.

pages.takeaway: The business added a third to its revenue in a year without adding to the cost of serving it.

pages.title: Every plan line is on or ahead of target except churn in small accounts
pages.notes: Do not read the table out. Point at the one line that is behind, churn in small accounts, and say the rest is on or ahead of target.
pages.head: Plan and actual, third quarter 2026
pages.takeaway: Churn is the one line that moved the wrong way.
points: The next section shows where and why

pages.title: Churn in small accounts doubled in a year while larger accounts held steady
pages.notes: This is the problem page. Small accounts doubled their churn in a year; larger accounts did not move. Pause here for questions before the options.
pages.takeaway: Two in five lost small accounts never finished setting up.
points: 62 small accounts cancelled in the quarter
pages.alt: Line chart of accounts lost each quarter as a share of accounts, by size. Small accounts rise from 2.1% to 4.2% over five quarters; mid-sized stay near 1.4% and large near 0.4%.
pages.source: Source: billing system and exit survey, 30 September 2026

pages.title: Guided onboarding costs less than a price cut and acts on the cause
pages.notes: Walk the options in the order shown and say why a price cut treats the symptom. Guided onboarding is the recommendation.

rows.label: What changes
values: A specialist sets up each new account

rows.label: Effect on churn
values: Small: price is the second reason

pages.title: Every new small account is set up with a specialist in four steps
pages.notes: Four steps, one sentence each. Say who owns each step, since that is the question the board will ask.

steps.name: Welcome call
steps.detail: On day one a specialist agrees with the account what it wants done first.

steps.name: Guided setup
steps.detail: In the first week the data is imported and the whole team is invited.

steps.name: First report together
steps.detail: By week three the account has built a report it will keep using.

steps.name: Health check
steps.detail: On day 60 usage is reviewed and anything that is stuck gets fixed.

pages.takeaway: No new small account is left to set itself up.

pages.title: The programme reaches every new small account by March 2027
pages.notes: Give the end date first, March 2027, then the milestone the board sees next.

steps.detail: The budget is released on the board's approval.
Every second new small account joins the pilot.
The pilot goes on only if churn is under 3%.

steps.what: Roll-out to all new small accounts
steps.detail: Existing accounts follow in the second half.

pages.title: The pilot is judged on three results the board will see in February
pages.notes: Name the three results and say when the board sees them. This is how the pilot is held to account.
pages.statement: The programme goes on only if the pilot shows that it works.

points.point: Churn among pilot accounts is under 3% a quarter
points.detail: Small accounts lost 4.2% in the third quarter; the plan for the year is 2.5%.

points.point: Nine in ten pilot accounts finish setup within a week
points.detail: Today six in ten do, and the accounts that do not are the ones that leave.

points.point: The cost stays within EUR 0.4 million for the year
points.detail: Two specialists and their tools, with no change to the price list.

pages.title: The board is asked for one approval; management owns the steps after it
pages.notes: State the one approval asked for. The steps after it are management's and need no decision today.

steps.action: Approve EUR 0.4 million for guided onboarding
steps.detail: The one decision asked of the board today.
Both start before the pilot does.

steps.action: Start the pilot with 40 new accounts
steps.detail: Every second new small account joins.

steps.action: Report pilot churn to the board
steps.detail: With the three results the pilot is judged on.

pages.title: One decision today: EUR 0.4 million for guided onboarding
pages.notes: Repeat the ask in one sentence and stop talking. Say whom to reach with questions after the meeting.
